X-Origin: Blair-L X-FileName: LBLAIR (Non-Privileged).pst Enron Global Technology is in the process of decommissioning the support for all non-standard Internet Email address formats. The only Internet Email address format that will be supported, once this effort is completed, is firstname.lastname@enron.com. We will no longer support Internet Email address formats such as name@enron.com, name@ect.enron.com, name@ei.enron.com (where "name" is an abbreviation, acronym or alternative to an employees firstname and/or lastname). Every Enron employee has an Internet Email address of firstname.lastname@enron.com and must begin making the necessary arrangements to start using this Internet address format if they are not using it already. Any new/existing application systems or business cards that reference a non-supported Internet Email address will need to be changed to reference the only supported firstname.lastname@enron.com Internet address format. It is important to remember to also notify any external contacts who are currently sending Internet email to any non-supported Internet Email addresses. To determine what your supported Internet Email address is, take your name as it appears in Outlook or Lotus Notes and replace any "spaces" that appear in your name with periods and append @enron.com. X-Origin: Blair-L X-FileName: LBLAIR (Non-Privileged).pst Pamela, I have 6 electronic tickets that were issued for travel on Continental on September 26 through the 28th, 2001. These travelers were to attend the Southern Gas Association (SGA) Energy Accounting and Marketing Services Conference in New Orleans. Due to the Terrorist attacks, the conference was cancelled. I realize the date 9/26/01 falls outside the deadline for allowing re-issuance of tickets with non-refundable fares without penalty or administrative fee. However, these Enron employees have asked me to approach Continental on their behalf and request that their tickets be re-issued to attend the conference on its rescheduled dates (January 16-18, 2002) without penalty. I will be happy to supply a copy of the cancellation/reschedule notice sent out by conference director, or any other supporting documentation that might suffice. The six travelers/ticket numbers/prices are as follows: BLAIR/GRACE LYNN / 005-7033562204 / $136.30 CALLANS/NANCY / 005-7033562205 / $136.30 MCDANIAL/JANET / 005-7033562232 / $136.30 JOHNSON/ALICE / 005-7033562301 / $136.30 HERNANDEZ/ALBERT / 005-7033562313 / $184.45 HANAGRIFF/RICHARD / 005-7033399204 / $104.75 Thank you in advance for anything you may be able to do to help these Enron travelers. X-Origin: Blair-L X-FileName: LBLAIR (Non-Privileged).pst Here are some thoughs on how we would account for the Offsystem Storage. Facts NNG moves 100,000 dts from physical inventory to Offsystem inventory. No accounting entry made to the G/L. I will look into Form 2 physical reporting changes. Offsystem inventory is reduced 2,000 dts to reflect in-kind fuel reduction. Case 1 In-Kind is replaced by simple purchase from 3rd party, NNG incurrs the cost. Debit 803 (Gas Purchases) or 858 (Fuel exp) 2,000 * cost of gas Credit A/P 2,000 * cost of gas Case 1 books all transactions outside of operational storage. Reducing the Offsystem storage will cause UAF to increase, however purchasing gas for Operational Storage and not recording it to Operational Storage will offset the UAF increase. Case 2 In-kind is replaced by Operational Storage, NNG incurrs the cost Debit 816 (Storage Fuel exp) 2,000 * MIP Credit 812 (Storage Fuel Credit) 2,000 * MIP Debit 808 (Storage Withdrawal) 2,000 * MIP Credit 1174 (Encroachment) 2,000 * MIP Case 3 In-kind is replaced by Operational Storage, Tracker incurrs the cost Debit 816 (Storage Fuel exp) 2,000 * MIP Credit 812 (Storage Fuel Credit) 2,000 * MIP Debit 808 (Storage Withdrawal)
